messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PROD ALERT: inference-queue-length metric for prod-west-1 exceeded 12k pending requests. GPU node pool failed to scale. Autoscaler status: 3 consecutive scale attempts failed. Paging on-call.

dave-oncall: on it. joining bridge now. can someone paste quick impact scope? which services?

carol-support: seeing spike in customer-visible errors; enterprise customers A & B reporting slow responses and 502s. Hits concentrated on /v1/generate endpoints.

mike-sre: queue growth started ~10:02 UTC, currently at 13,200 pending. Pod backlog in ns=infra-inference. Many pods Pending with "0/" allocatable GPUs.

jin-mlinfra: looking at cluster autoscaler logs — seeing repeated failures creating nodes. Copying relevant excerpt:

```
I0612 10:05:24.123456 1 scale_up.go:412] NodeGroup prod-gpu-ng: attempted scale up to 0 -> 8 (max 8)
E0612 10:05:24.789012 1 aws_manager.go:233] createAutoScalingGroup failed: UnauthorizedOperation: You are not authorized to perform: iam:PassRole
	status code: 403, request id: abcdefg-1234
```

mike-sre: aws ASG create attempts returning 403 PassRole. That explains nodes failing at creation time — autoscaler retries but AMI/launch-template requires PassRole to attach instance profile.

lia-eng: also noticed new launch template version was rolled last night during a config push. It references instanceProfile arn:aws:iam::123456789012:instance-profile/redwood-gpu-role-v2. Perhaps role change didn't propagate to the autoscaler role.

ops-bot: Related alert: iam-audit-bot detected recent change to IAM policy redwood-autoscaler-role at 2026-06-12T02:30:00Z.

dave-oncall: immediate mitigation? can we manually provision nodes with a launch template that uses the old profile or a role that autoscaler can PassRole with?

jin-mlinfra: yes. Plan A: create a temporary nodegroup (manual ASG) using LT version that uses instance profile redwood-gpu-role (v1). I'll run the ASG create with an account admin key in a maintenance window tag. This should bypass autoscaler PassRole if we create ASG directly (we need an account user that can CreateAutoScalingGroup). If ASG created, nodes will join and pods can schedule (taints permitting).

mike-sre: also noticing many Pending pods show nodeSelector tolerations but pods stuck on taint: gpu-reserved=true:NoSchedule. The taint is set by bootstrap config in the new LT. We might need to make sure the kubelet bootstraps with correct labels/taints.

lia-eng: if we bring nodes up manually, we can also set `kubectl taint nodes <node> gpu-reserved-` to remove the NoSchedule taint so inference pods can land.

sre-lead: assign roles: jin (mlinfra) execute manual ASG create, mike (sre) will remove taint on new nodes and monitor queue drain, dave will coordinate comms and bridge.

jin-mlinfra: starting manual ASG create now, using older launch template version 3 (verified) and instance-profile redwood-gpu-role-v1.

```
aws autoscaling create-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name temp-prod-gpu-burst-1778 \
  --launch-template LaunchTemplateId=lt-0abcd1234,Version=3 --min-size 2 --max-size 8 --desired-capacity 4 --vpc-zone-identifier "subnet-xxx"
```

mike-sre: ASG create returned success, instances launching. kubelet logs show nodes registering.

ops-bot: New nodes registering: ip-10-12-34-56, ip-10-12-34-57, ip-10-12-34-58, ip-10-12-34-59

mike-sre: nodes came up with taint `gpu-reserved=true:NoSchedule` — removing taint to allow immediate scheduling for existing inference pods.

```
kubectl get nodes -l node-role.kubernetes.io/gpu=true -o name
kubectl taint nodes ip-10-12-34-56 gpu-reserved- || true
kubectl taint nodes ip-10-12-34-57 gpu-reserved- || true
```

mike-sre: pods are scheduling. queue dropping from 13.2k -> 4.8k in the first 6 minutes. Token consumption ramping up. :thumbsup:

dave-oncall: calling out to customers: posted in #customer-impact to notify affected customers we have temporary capacity added and are mitigating; asking for any ongoing errors. (message id: msg-992)

carol-support: customers A & B confirm latency improved but some messages still retrying on their side. We'll keep them updated.

jin-mlinfra: while manual ASG fixes immediate impact, root cause remains: autoscaler role lost PassRole permission when IAM policy rotated. Need follow-ups:
- Restore iam:PassRole for redwood-autoscaler-role to allow autoscaler to call CreateLaunchTemplate/CreateAutoScalingGroup with instance profiles.
- Validate launch template rollout automation so it doesn't reference new instance profile until autoscaler can pass role.
- Add canary test: autoscaler CreateASG simulation after LT rollouts.

sre-lead: agreed. Also add a guard to block launch-template promotion if it changes instance-profile ARN without coordination with infra-iam.

mike-sre: verifying no other failures: kube events show some ImagePullBackOffs for a GPU node — those are limited. overall P99 latency for /v1/generate down from 3.2s -> 1.1s since nodes added.

dave-oncall: is autoscaler healthy now? it will likely continue to attempt creating nodes but should succeed once IAM fix is in. For now temp ASG will handle load.

jin-mlinfra: scheduling a quick-priority fix to re-grant PassRole to redwood-autoscaler-role and then we can let autoscaler scale normally. Raising PR now (internal iam repo). Tagged: @infra-iam for expedited review.

ops-bot: PR created: infra/iam#452 - grant iam:PassRole to redwood-autoscaler-role — review requested from infra-iam.

lia-eng: once PassRole restored, recommend trigger a dry-run scale by setting max nodes +1 to confirm successful ASG creation then revert.

carol-support: will update customers with ETA 20-30m for full normalization. they asked for RCA when complete.

sre-lead: post-incident tasks (owner, due):
- restore PassRole (jin) - in flight
- add integration test for LT -> autoscaler compatibility (mike) - 3d
- add pre-promotion gating for instance-profile changes (lia) - 5d
- prod postmortem doc (dave) - 2d

mike-sre: queue at 800 now and trending down. marking incident as mitigated but not resolved. keep bridge open for 30m monitoring.

dave-oncall: thanks everyone. checking out of the bridge to coordinate comms. will reopen if queue spikes. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident severity lowered to SEV2 — mitigation in place. Automated follow-ups scheduled.

sre-lead: final note: no data loss, customers experienced degraded latency and error spikes. we'll include timeline + IAM policy churn details in postmortem. Closing handoff to infra-iam and devops to implement long-term fixes.
